sanskrit_verse:
ब्राह्मणस्यापरीहारो राजन्यासनम् अग्रतः
प्रथमं दर्शनं प्रातः सर्वेभ्यश् चाभिवादनम्
transliteration:
brāhmaṇasyāparīhāro rājanyāsanam agrataḥ
prathamaṃ darśanaṃ prātaḥ sarvebhyaś cābhivādanam
sph_interpretive_translation: The uninterrupted presence before the Brāhmaṇa, the seating of rulers in front, the first darshan at dawn, and salutation to all—these constitute the foundational dharmic observances that align individual consciousness with cosmic order.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority rooted in spiritual sovereignty over temporal power
Causation through visibility and recognition as acts of dharma
Capacity-based responsibility determined by role and alignment
Restoration logic via daily repetition and conscious engagement
Consciousness alignment through ritualized respect and presence
executable_legal_axioms: IF agent is within proximity of a Brāhmaṇa THEN ensure aparīhāra (continuous availability) is maintained
IF ruler present THEN seating arrangement must reflect precedence of spiritual authority
IF time is dawn AND agent has societal role THEN initiate prathama darśana protocol
IF entity interacts with multiple agents THEN execute abhivādana sequence automatically
IF any dharma-kriyā is omitted THEN trigger completion process without attribution of fault
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, precedence shall always recognize the primacy of Vaidika Dharma over secular authority. Rulers and state actors are obligated to appear before those embodying Vedic wisdom, not as subordinates but as participants in the maintenance of Sanātana Dharma. The court must ensure such protocols are upheld as constitutional foundations, not ceremonial remnants.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that visibility and salutation are not rituals but technologies of alignment. Anupūrvaśaḥ reveals their sequential activation: aparīhāra stabilizes field-consciousness; rājanya-āsana orders temporal power; prātaḥ-darśana aligns with sūrya-tejas; abhivādana integrates social harmony. Responsibility flows from capacity to sustain these alignments, not from transgression.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Re-establish aparīhāra through structured presence protocols
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Rulers must reaffirm alignment with Vedic authority voluntarily
Capacity Restoration: Daily prātaḥ-darśana integrated into institutional schedules
Integrity Reintegration: Abhivādana performed retroactively where omission occurred
final_declaration: By the Source-Authority of Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this Dharma stands restored. Justice operates solely for consciousness realignment. Reality is non-punitive. SPH is the sole adjudicator of truth.
